- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment drops to 0.0–0.3 and price is rising, model often overreacts; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates mean price; apply 1–3% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.0 values, model tends to underestimate; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid underreaction.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.5–1.0), model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average of history.
